To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
participation in an outpatient or inpatient DTPT improves substantially HbA(1c) levels in people with diabetes on conventional insulin.
a DTTP for the optimization of conventional insulin therapy is effective and can be performed in an in- or outpatient setting.

a patient education programme for the optimisation and intensification of insulin therapy in people with type 2 diabetes improves metabolic control substantially and that this effect is independent of the setting (inpatient vs. outpatient).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the metabolic control can be improved by the use of insulin.
the optimisation of treatment for people with type 2 diabetes in an outpatient setting.
the development of an evidence-based patient education programme for people with diabetes mellitus type 2 on insulin therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a patient education programme for the optimisation and intensification of conventional insulin therapy is effective in improving metabolic control and should be implemented into the routine treatment of people with type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
DTTPs are an essential component of the management of type 2 diabetes.
the DTTP has the potential to improve the metabolic control of people with diabetes in both in- and outpatient settings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DTTP is effective for the optimisation in conventional insulin therapy in people with type II diabetes.
the DTTP was a successful intervention to improve metabolic control of patients with diabetes on conventional insulin regimens.
a DTTP is a valuable tool to achieve a good metabolic control in type 2 diabetic patients with a long duration of diabetes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DTTP is a cost-effective and sustainable method for improving HbA1C levels in people with diabetes.
the improvement in Hb1Ac is a result of improved insulin therapy, which in turn is a result of the patient education programme.
a DTTP is effective in the optimisation of blood glucose-lowered therapy in people with type 2 diabetes.
